title: 25th Sitting of second session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 under the Speaker with routine business: attendance, the agenda, two committee-related announcements and a rules matter sent to the General Committee. A government bill to amend the Income Tax Act (Law 2019/25), which raises withholding tax on payments to contractors not registered in the Maldives from 5% to 10%, had its first reading and a long preliminary debate; members across the floor argued over whether it levels the field for Maldivian contractors, with side arguments about enforcement, spending and basic services. The chair closed the debate and said the bill would go to a vote at vote time, so no vote count appears in this part. After a recess (10:29 to 11:02) the House began debating Dr Ahmed Shamheed's resolution on the Maldives Pearl Residence Program, and the part ends while he is still speaking. The text is readable but garbled in places. The sitting continued the debate on Dr. Ahmed Shamheed's resolution calling for the 'Maldives Palm Residence Programme' (permanent residence for foreigners) to stop and its agreements to be disclosed; government-aligned speakers argued against it and no vote on it is recorded in this part. Committee reports followed on the Waste Management Act, National Payment System Act and Utility Regulatory Authority Act amendment bills, with the utility report drawing a debate about island water, sewerage and power services. After a 20-minute pause for voting-system problems, all four votes went the same way: the waste, payment-system and utility bills passed (64-0, 66-0 and 61-6) and the Income Tax Act amendment bill was accepted 64-1 and sent to the whole-House committee. The chair adjourned until 9:00 on Tuesday 18 August 2026.

items.outcome: 4 votes taken; Income Tax Act (2019/25) amendment bill accepted 64-1 and sent to the whole-House committee, 3 bills passed

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill as useful for local contractors, small and medium businesses, and state income.
Raised a point of order saying the township the Kendhoo member mentioned was granted under the MDP, not this government; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.
Argued the resolution was not warranted and that the Noonu Atoll SEZ development benefits Holhudhoo residents, including the island's economy.
Said the resolution should be removed from the House and criticised the MDP-era handling of atoll land.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said his constituency lacks water and sewerage despite large state revenues, and asked what benefit the people get.
Said taxes can be raised but the government must cut its own spending for this to work.
Said Kunahandhoo has had no water and sewerage work and Hithadhoo has only one generator, asking for services alongside the utility bills.
After the chair reminded members to refer to each other by constituency, said the service shortfalls are a serious issue, not a joke.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said critics' arguments went against the bill's purpose, and explained it closes a gap where large foreign contractors paid little tax compared with local firms.
Called the resolution's premise inaccurate, saying the SEZ law offers investment tiers and the residence programme does not give foreigners citizens' rights; compared it with MDP-era visas.
On the utility bill, said the committee studied it thoroughly and defended the government's record on island generators and services.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said tax was criticised by today's government side when the MDP introduced it, and pointed to the sale of land in a special economic zone township.
Argued the bill will not help Maldivian contractors who are owed payment while big state projects go to foreign firms.
Objected to how the agenda was handled and was reminded by the chair to debate the bill before him.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill as removing an imbalance between local and outside contractors, and welcomed the rise from 5% to 10%.
Presented the Finance Committee report on the National Payment System Act amendment, which sets up a national payment switch and strengthens payment-system governance and monitoring.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said withholding tax falls on outside firms and not Maldivians, questioned the effect on small guesthouses, and doubted it would give locals more work.
Said revenue has risen since the 2019 change and he expects more, but his concern is where the money ends up.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: On the tax bill, said 10% alone will not win locals contracts and asked for a required share of sub-contracting (30 to 50%) for Maldivians.
Introduced his resolution on the Maldives Pearl Residence Program: asked what the state gains from the Henley and Partners agreement and raised national security concerns.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the amendment and thanked the sponsor, saying it closes routes through which money leaves the country.
Raised a point of order that the Maavashu member was not speaking on the bill; the chair asked him to stay on the bill and to refer to members by constituency.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said extra revenue means little while his constituency lacks power, water and sewerage, and criticised how quickly the bill moved through the House.
On the utility bill, said residents in his constituency still wait years for water, sewerage and power connections and urged action on those delays.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Introduced the bill: raises withholding tax on payments to unregistered foreign contractors from 5% to 10% so local firms compete on equal terms.
Said it adds no tax for ordinary people or small businesses and asked for quick passage.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, saying a clear 10% withholding tax would bring more money to the state from large foreign contractors.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Thanked the sponsor and said the bill targets outside contractors, not local small firms or ordinary people, and urged members not to oppose it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the amendment as a step forward for local contractors, saying foreign contractors should not pay less tax than Maldivian firms.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said the bill's wording should be explained clearly, supported raising the rate gradually, and urged patience before locals see opportunities.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Supported the bill, urged members not to politicise it, and said taxes on outside contractors should be raised step by step.

speakers.name: Ali Ashrag
positions: Fully supported the bill, saying foreign contractors take large profits abroad and the change ends that unfairness without taxing small local businesses.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill as needed to put Maldivian and foreign contractors on equal terms, and said some criticism aims to mislead the public.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said a higher withholding tax helps only if enforced, and asked how it will be collected, citing dollar sales and a resort licensed with money still owed.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Presented the Environment and Climate Change Committee report on the Utility Regulatory Authority Act amendment; no public comments or ministry comments were received, so it was sent for passage.

decisions: Committee membership changes announced: Hussain Ziyad to the Economic Committee, Mauroof Zakir to the Decentralisation Committee (dated 16 August 2026).
Decentralisation Committee's deadline for the bill amending the Decentralisation Act announced as 20 August 2026.
Mohamed Mamdooh's matter on removing clause (l) of Rule 257-1 sent to the General Committee for study.
First reading of the government bill amending the Income Tax Act (Law 2019/25) read.
Preliminary debate on the bill closed; chair said it would be put to a vote at vote time.
Recess from 10:29 to 11:02, then the sitting resumed under the Speaker.
Waste Management Act (2022/24) amendment bill passed, 64-0.
National Payment System Act (2021/8) amendment bill passed, 66-0.
Utility Regulatory Authority Act (2020/26) amendment bill passed, 61-6.
Income Tax Act (2019/25) amendment bill accepted 64-1 and sent to the whole-House committee.
Voting was paused 13:44-14:04 because of technical problems with members' voting systems.
Sitting adjourned until 9:00 on Tuesday 18 August 2026.

votes.what: Income Tax Act (2019/25) amendment bill (Hassan Zareer, Mathiveri): accept and send to the whole-House committee
Waste Management Act (2022/24) amendment bill (Ibrahim Shifaz, Ungoofaaru): pass
National Payment System Act (2021/8) amendment bill (Mohamed Shahid, Hulhudhoo): pass
Utility Regulatory Authority Act (2020/26) amendment bill (Hassan Waheed, Vilifushi): pass
